viewer_sees: MACRO OBJECT — the corroded fragment hanging in dark water, one gear tooth catching a glint of surface light; then the same fragment on black with a faint golden ghost of the complete dial drawn over it
a tiny single-masted sponge boat heeling under a black squall between towering waves; the boat slipping into the lee of Antikythera's bare limestone cliffs
from below the surface: the diver's copper helmet and weighted boots sinking into blue, the boat's hull a small dark shape on the bright water above, the air hose a line between them

SILHOUETTE — through murk, human and horse shapes lying tangled on the slope, outlines only, seen past the diver's helmet porthole close to camera; the crew on deck crowding around the diver as his helmet comes off, faces frightened
the reveal: a light shaft falls across a bronze arm and a marble horse head half-buried in sand, the bodies are statues; wider, the whole debris field around ancient hull timbers and spilled amphorae

PROCESS / CUTAWAY — a vertical section of the sea: navy ship and sponge boat on top, hose and rope running down to divers roping a bronze statue into a sling at the bottom; two men on deck turning the brass pump wheel
EMPTY AFTERMATH — an empty copper helmet resting on a coil of rope on the deck, a canvas suit lying flat beside it, evening light
LEDGER / ACCUMULATION — museum tables filling with finds, statues, glass, pottery in rows; at the edge of one table a nondescript green lump on a tray with no label, ignored
the lump split into pieces on the tray; Stais leaning in with a magnifying glass; MACRO — a single hand-cut gear wheel emerging from the crust
PROCESS / CUTAWAY — the fragment drawn as a translucent layered section, gear stacked behind gear inside it; the fragments laid out inside the faint outline of a shoebox-sized case
scholars in 1900s suits arguing over the table, one pointing at the fragment, another shaking his head; the fragment alone on a velvet tray, unlabelled
the fragment in a dim display case gathering dust; an X-ray scan view, glowing blue-white gears and rows of tiny Greek letters appearing out of solid crust
the restored mechanism, bright bronze, on an ancient Greek workshop table; a hand on the side crank; the gear train seen through the open case with a star map glowing faintly above it
MACRO OBJECT — the front dial, zodiac ring, Sun and Moon pointers; close on the small half-silver half-black moon-phase ball
the back plate with its two great spiral dials; a moon sliding across a darkening sun over a Greek city; runners in the stadium at Olympia
a Greek astronomer on a rooftop at night marking the Moon against the stars on a wax tablet; a string of moon positions spaced unevenly across the sky
PROCESS / CUTAWAY — two gears on offset axles, a pin riding in a slot, drawn large and clear like a technical illustration; the moon pointer on the dial in its fast and slow positions
TIMELINE — a long road of history: the mechanism at the near end, a vast empty dark stretch, a medieval cathedral astronomical clock tiny at the far end
the corroded fragment alone in its museum case, lit from above, a visitor's reflection faint in the glass
Cicero writing by lamplight on a scroll; Archimedes in Syracuse beside a bronze sphere of rings; the ancient sphere and the restored mechanism side by side
empty pegs and dust outlines on the shelf of an ancient workshop where other mechanisms once stood; a foundry crucible glowing, bronze objects melting into it
the ancient ship going down in a storm off the cliffs, cargo tumbling through blue water; the fragment resting in sand on the dark seabed under one faint shaft of light, fish passing
END CARD — the restored mechanism and the corroded fragment side by side on deep blue, channel end card
